Andahuaylillas lies on the road from Cusco toward Puno. The settlement's main landmark is the Church of San Pedro Apóstol on the central square. Its modest exterior contrasts with the richly decorated interior, which features paintings, ornamental details and altars.

The church makes Andahuaylillas an important stop on a cultural route through the southern Andes. A visit offers an introduction to colonial religious art in a small rural settlement. The square and surrounding mountain slopes add to the experience.

Angra dos Reis lies on the Atlantic coast of Rio de Janeiro State, approximately 155 km south of Rio. Travelers come here for the Costa Verde, where green slopes descend to the sea and the bay is dotted with islands and small coves.

From the port, you can take a catamaran, small boat or yacht out to sea. The route is usually planned around swimming, island stops and an unhurried day on the water. If you wish, the boat trip can be combined with a hotel stay and activities along the coast.

Angra is already part of Ada Tours' programs for corporate groups: it is possible to combine land-based activities with a private boat, catamaran, catering and an evening event. For individual travelers, the region is a natural extension of Rio and connects well with Ilha Grande or Paraty.

### Antigua Guatemala — Witness to Colonial Grandeur!

Antigua Guatemala is one of the oldest and most beautiful cities in Central America. A testament to Spain's colonial grandeur, with its cobbled streets, beautiful buildings and classical architecture, Antigua is included on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

In Antigua Guatemala, visitors can see restored monuments of Spanish colonial architecture, including the Church of Saint Francis, dating from 1579 and one of the city's oldest churches, spend time at the central Parque Central square and visit a number of museums.

## Antigua — An Exotic Corner of Guatemala

### Antigua — A Bright Flower of Guatemala!

The city was repeatedly destroyed by earthquakes, the most devastating of which occurred in 1773. After that event, the city never fully recovered and lost its former importance. Antigua is strikingly picturesque against the backdrop of its three impressive surrounding volcanoes. The surviving colonial-era buildings, which have weathered many earthquakes, floods and fires, lend the city its distinctive atmosphere. With its streets and squares, and intricate patterns of varied tropical flowers and plants, Antigua itself seems like a bright flower.
